top.strength: Where Plato puts it: known, it is in his text. A real place behind it: none found. Each place proposed since: guessed.

slot.what: Where people have looked for Atlantis, on today's map. Plato gives only a direction, in his own words: an island outside the Pillars of Heracles, in the Atlantic. Each ring is a claim, with who made it and when. None has been proven.
slot.alt: A map of the North Atlantic and the Mediterranean today, north at the top. A box in the ocean west of the Strait of Gibraltar quotes Plato: outside the pillars of Heracles, an island in front of the straits, larger than Libya and Asia put together. Dashed rings mark places proposed for Atlantis, each with who proposed it and when: the Doñana marshes in southern Spain (Schulten 1922, Kühne 2004), the Spartel Bank in the Strait (Díaz-Montexano 2000, Collina-Girard 2001), the Richat Structure in Mauritania (a video of 2018), Thera, now Santorini (Figuier 1872), the Azores (Donnelly 1882), the Bimini Road in the Bahamas (Marx and Rebikoff 1969) and Heligoland (Spanuth 1953). An arrow at the bottom points to Antarctica (Barbiero 1974, Flem-Ath 1995). None of these claims is proven.

blocks.nav: Where did Plato say Atlantis was?
blocks.h: Where did Plato say Atlantis was?
paras: In the Atlantic Ocean, on an island outside the Pillars of Heracles. In the Timaeus an Egyptian priest tells Solon of an island "larger than Libya and Asia put together", "situated in front of the straits" that the Greeks called the Pillars of Heracles, while the sea inside them is "only a harbour" (Timaeus 24e to 25a). Every quote here is from

The end of the island "towards the pillars of Heracles" faced "the region of Gades", today's Cádiz (Critias 114b). Its city stood near the sea, in a plain Plato gives as 3,000 by 2,000 stadia, roughly 550 by 370 kilometres, facing south (Critias 118a to b). On the reading of the classicist
, that puts the capital at least several hundred kilometres from the Strait. In the story the island then sank, so the text gives a direction and a size, never a spot on today's map.
The Pillars were the headlands of the Strait of Gibraltar: the Rock of Gibraltar, and on the African side Jebel Musa or Monte Hacho,
. The classical Greek writers known to us seem to have put them there, the geologist Jacques Collina-Girard argues and Nesselrath agrees.

No. The Richat Structure in Mauritania, also called the Eye of the Sahara or the Eye of Africa, is a natural dome of rock about 40 kilometres across, pushed up by molten rock that cooled about 100 million years ago, as the
describes it. Wind and water wore it down into rings,
explains.
The Atlantis claim spread in 2018 through a YouTube video that news media widely reported, the

records. The rings recall the "alternate zones of sea and land" of Plato's city (Critias 113d), but not his numbers: his rings come to about 27 stadia, some 5 kilometres, and with the wall he sets 50 stadia beyond them to about 127 stadia, some 23 kilometres, by our sum (Critias 115e to 117e), against the Richat's 40. His city lay by the sea, and the Richat lies about 500 kilometres from the coast,
notes. No trace of a city or a canal has been found there, the
records.
Most scholars say no. An eruption about 1600 BC, whose date is debated, destroyed the town of Akrotiri on Thera, today's Santorini, but
the link with Atlantis.
The first known to make the link was Louis Figuier, in 1872, the

records, and Spyridon Marinatos, who dug Akrotiri from 1967, became its leading voice. Some geologists still make the link: the eruption may have helped end Minoan civilisation, "leaving its imprint on Greek mythology", the
says, and it names Atlantis.

But Thera lies inside the Mediterranean, not outside the Pillars, and the eruption came about 1,000 years before Solon, not 9,000. Even Collina-Girard, who places Atlantis by Gibraltar, finds that neither the place nor the date fits,
reports.

blocks.nav: What other places have been proposed for Atlantis?
blocks.h: What other places have been proposed for Atlantis?
paras: Dozens, most of them in or near the Mediterranean, and none has been shown to be Plato's island,
sums up.

points: Southern Spain, near Cádiz.
Adolf Schulten placed Atlantis there in 1922. In 2004 Rainer Kühne, prompted by Werner Wickboldt, described
on satellite images of the Doñana marshes. Whether they are natural is not known,
reports, adding that geologists found the area was a gulf of the sea, with no island big enough for a village, until the Middle Ages.
The Spartel Bank, in the Strait.
In 2001 Collina-Girard proposed an island there that the sea drowned at the end of the last Ice Age, close to Plato's date. At its largest it measured only about 14 by 5 kilometres,
notes. Its top now lies 52 to 56 metres down, so it forms none of the shallows Plato describes, and Collina-Girard "has not found Plato's Atlantis",
concludes.
The Azores.

Ignatius Donnelly took them in 1882 for the mountain tops of Atlantis. They are "volcanic islands and are not the remnants of a more or less large continental mass", Charles Schuchert concluded in 1917,
quotes him, and some of them have risen, not sunk.
The Bimini Road, Bahamas.

Divers found this line of stone blocks in 1968, and Robert Marx and Dimitri Rebikoff headlined it "Atlantis at Last?" in 1969. Geologists and archaeologists agree it is natural beachrock, its shells about 3,500 radiocarbon years old, the
reports.
Antarctica.

Flavio Barbiero in 1974 and Rand and Rose Flem-Ath in 1995 placed Atlantis there, as a land that a sudden shift of the Earth's crust moved to the pole, where ice buried it. But its ice began to form about 34 million years ago,
reports.
Heligoland.
Jürgen Spanuth in 1953 put Atlantis beside the island and had it destroyed in the Bronze Age, around 1200 BC, the overviews in
and
record, thousands of years after Plato's date.

paras: From Plato's text, the only source, and from what geology and archaeology have found at each place proposed.

The text sets three tests. The place is outside the Pillars, in the Atlantic. The date is 9,000 years before Solon, about 9600 BC by our count. The size is an island larger than Libya and Asia together. Measured against them, Santorini misses the place and the date, the Spartel Bank and the Richat Structure the size, and the Azores and Antarctica fail on their own geology.

paras: He put it outside the Pillars of Heracles, in the Atlantic. The Mediterranean is his "harbour".
His 9,000 years before Solon date the war with Athens. The island sank "some time afterwards", at a time Plato does not give, Nesselrath points out.

subs.h: "The Richat Structure is an impact crater."
paras: It was first taken for one, but field studies in the 1960s found no sign of an impact. It is a dome worn down by erosion.
They show two rectangles in the Doñana marshes, reported in 2004. Whether they are natural is not known.
